subject: Borderless plotting with ggplot2 - how to remove the pixel border on the right side and the bottom?

messages.author: 5d004bc59a87a5f3
messages.subject: Borderless plotting with ggplot2 - how to remove the pixel border on the right side and the bottom?
parts:
Hello everybody,

I am aware that related topics have been around for a while, but actually I was not able to find a solution for my specific case. My goal is to plot in ggplot2 without any borders or margins - the best I could achieve so far comes with a 1px wide (white) border on the right side and the bottom.
Basically,it is the panel border that peeks out at the right side and the bottom (I think); see the plot output attached for an example. I think there must be a way to hide this contour. Unfortunately, the colorization of the panel border or the rectangle border is not really an option for my acutal work.

Here's the code, I would appreciate any form of help:

>>
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)

datapoly <- data.frame(
  x = c(0,1,1,0),
  y = c(0,0,1,1)
)

theme_blank <- list(theme(  axis.text.x       = element_blank(), # (text)
                            axis.text.y       = element_blank(), # (text)
                            axis.title.x      = element_blank(), # (text)
                            axis.title.y      = element_blank(), # (text)
                            axis.line         = element_blank(), # (segment)
                            axis.ticks        = element_blank(), # (segment)
                            axis.ticks.length = unit(0,"npc"), # (unit)
                            axis.ticks.margin = unit(0,"npc"), # (unit)
                            
                            legend.background = element_blank(), # (rect)
                            legend.key        = element_blank(), # (rect)
                            legend.key.size   = unit(0,"npc"), # (unit)
                            legend.key.width  = unit(0,"npc"), # (unit)
                            legend.text       = element_blank(), # (text)
                            legend.title      = element_blank(), # (text)
                            #legend.title.align   # (?)
                            #legend.position      # (?)
                            #legend.justification # (?)
                            #legend.direction     # (?)
                            #legend.box           # (?)
  
                            panel.background  = element_blank(), # (rect)
                            panel.border      = element_blank(), # (rect)
                            panel.margin      = unit(0,"npc"), # (unit)
                            panel.grid.major  = element_blank(), # (line)
                            panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(), # (line)
                            #plot.background   = element_blank(), # (rect)
                            plot.background = element_rect(colour = "red", fill = "green", size = 1, linetype=3), # Added for illustrative reasons 
                            title = element_blank(), # (see plot.title)
                            plot.title = element_blank(), # (text) 
                            plot.margin = unit(c(0,0,0,0), "npc") #top, right, bottom, left
))


# Alternative solution (with the same problem) from: http://www.r-bloggers.com/a-replacement-for-theme_blank/ 
# cf. https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/New-theme-system
new_theme_empty <- theme_bw()
new_theme_empty$line <- element_blank()
new_theme_empty$rect <- element_blank()
new_theme_empty$strip.text <- element_blank()
new_theme_empty$axis.text <- element_blank()
new_theme_empty$plot.title <- element_blank()
new_theme_empty$axis.title <- element_blank()
new_theme_empty$plot.margin <- structure(c(0, 0, -1, -1), unit = "lines", valid.unit = 3L, class = "unit")



plot <- ggplot(datapoly, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_polygon(fill="blue") +
  guides(fill=F) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) + scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x=NULL, y=NULL, ggtitle=NULL) + 
  theme_blank

plot

#ggsave("plot.png", width = 5, height = 5)
<<

Best, Chris
